newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Supported despite thin talk.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Supported despite thin talk.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market held steady on Monday amid a lack of fresh factors but sentiment was supported, traders said.
Tightening supplies over the upcoming summer months were expected to boost prices, but there were very few bids as many players were staying on the sidelines, they said.
Kuwait traditionally exports fewer cargoes in the summer due to higher domestic demand while some South Korean refineries are still in maintaintenance shutdown, also reducing supplies, traders said.
The market is waiting for results of two import tender from Taiwan and South Korea, closing on Wednesday and Thursday respectively.
"Nothing is happening. It is very quiet," one trader said.
Although the cargo market was little changed, bunker suppliers complained that supported cargo prices have dampened the already weak bunker market.
"Bunker demand is so poor that we can not raise offers, but at the same time cargo prices are supported, which makes it very difficult for us," said one bunker supplier.
Bunker 380-cst grade was quoted at $95/$97 per tonne, $2/$3 per tonne higher than the cargo level. The spread is normally $6 per tonne.
In the swaps market, July swaps edged up slightly to $100.00/$100.75 per tonne from last Friday's $99.75/$100.50. August swaps were unchanged at $99.25/$100.00.
By late Monday, SIMEX fuel oil futures contract reamined untraded. The July contract was bid/offered at $99.80/$101.50.
